items.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998
items.q: Eddie called me three days later and he says, 'We’d like to have you on the band,' I started to cry.

ctx.x: And jazz. Can you recall the first listening experience with either of those with jazz that registered on you?

Well it’s hard to pin down except I remember specifically hearing Benny Goodman play “Benny Rides Again” a new arrangement by Eddie Sauter, when I was in high school. And when I got the call in Rochester from a woman who identified herself as from the Willard Alexander Agency, it was really Kay Finegan, Bill Finegan’s wife, about auditioning for the Sauter-Finegan Orchestra, of course I was elated beyond expectation to hear that, because that’s the greatest band that ever happened. And I started to rave about…
You didn’t know that you were talking to his wife.
